title: Step-by-Step Configuration Guide for Authentication Service

blocks.text: This article provides the recommended configuration steps to begin using Authentication Service for your organization.
Authentication Service recommends using the following Zscaler Client Connector versions for new deployments:

blocks.item: Zscaler Client Connector for Windows 4.8
Zscaler Client Connector for macOS 4.8
Zscaler Client Connector for iOS 4.4.4
Zscaler Client Connector for Android 4.1
Zscaler Client Connector for Linux 4.2.1
Step 1: Sign In to the Zscaler Admin Console
To sign in to the Zscaler Admin Console, see Signing in to the Zscaler Admin Console.
Step 2: Sync Domains
Ensure that all the required domains are available on the Domains page (Administration > Authentication > Domains).
See image.
Domains are automatically synced from Internet & SaaS (ZIA) and Private Access (ZPA) every 24 hours.
Step 3: Add Users to Authentication Service
You can add users using one of the following methods:
Integrate Authentication Service with an External IdP.
Add users as hosted users to Authentication Service.
(Optional) To allow admins to use FIDO as the primary authenticator without the password requirement, enable the Allow FIDO2 as Primary Authenticator option on the Authentication Methods page.
(Optional) To prompt users for MFA enrollment during authentication, enable the Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) for Service Enrollment option on the Authentication Methods page.
All admins, including the super admin (admin@xxxxx.net), must enroll an MFA authenticator after initially setting up their password.
Step 4: Configure Authentication Session Controls (Optional)

To enable more controls, such as the administrator’s Idle Session Timeout, Authentication Session for Service Enrollment, and Force Authentication for Private Access Reauthentication, see Configuring the Authentication Session.
Step 5: Update Password Policies (Optional)
To modify the password policy configuration to comply with your organization’s requirements, see Configuring the Password Policy.
Step 6: Configure Admin Sign-On Policies (Optional)
To create rules to allow or deny access from a specific location, see Configuring Admin Sign-On Policy. The Admin Sign-On policies are created using IP locations or IP location groups.
Step 7: Create Custom Roles (Optional)
To create custom roles in Authentication Service for role-based access control for Authentication Service administrators, see Adding Authentication Service Admin Roles.

If your organization uses Unified Role-Based Access Control (RBAC), administrator roles for Authentication Service and some Zscaler services are managed on a different Role Management page. To learn more, see About Role Management. Unified RBAC is a feature in limited availability. To access Unified RBAC, contact your Zscaler Account team.
Step 8: Assign Entitlements to Users and User Groups

To assign administrative entitlement and make the user an admin to Authentication Service or other services such as Internet & SaaS, Private Access, etc., see Assigning Entitlements to Users and User Groups.
To assign service entitlement to allow users to enroll to Zscaler services such as Internet & SaaS, Private Access, etc., see Assigning Entitlements to Users and User Groups.
Step 9: Configure Step-Up Authentication (Optional)

To provide resource-specific, risk-based access to users, you can configure step-up authentication with external IdPs. Ensure that you have configured the necessary authentication levels in Authentication Service and access policies in supported Zscaler services. Users must have Authentication Service access to configure step-up authentication. To learn more, see Understanding Step-Up Authentication and Configuring Authentication Levels.
Authentication Service with User Single Sign-On (SSO) is required to enable step-up authentication for the tenant. For further assistance, contact Zscaler Support.
